purpose: Durable rotation registry for recovered and active long-form Warhammer 40K chronicles. Recovery backlog takes priority over new continuation work. Once recovered material is indexed and verified, rotate between distinct existing story lines rather than repeatedly extending one arc.

policy.chapterCapRule: Hard cap of 40 chapters per book. A continuing story that reaches Chapter XL must close that book at or before Chapter XL; further narrative continues as a subsequent book rather than Chapter XLI.

active.title: The Long Patrol of Broussard
active.sourceDocument: The Long Patrol of Broussard — Working Draft
active.recoveredThrough: X. THE FORWARD HOLDS — complete through Broussard organizing the search for Jerrik Noll, Edren Vale and Pallas Dorn and ending: “Let’s go find them.”
active.sourceObservedThrough: X. THE FORWARD HOLDS — complete; the connected Google working draft contains no later chapter.
active.currentEndpoint: XIII. THE THING UNDER THE ICE — a large High Presidio predator breaches the recovery perimeter and attacks Chimera Two before moving beneath the stranded Hesperant Vale. Broussard uses the four Chimeras as a controlled fire channel, refuses pursuit onto fractured ice, releases the recovery hauler from its tow rig before the predator can use the connection against the ship, and kills the animal when it resurfaces. Chimera Two remains mobile with a destroyed vision block and minor track damage; no additional personnel are lost. The predator takes much of the tow alignment into the broken ice, and the ship repair estimate slips to roughly thirty-seven hours. The fourteen-second telemetry anomaly remains untouched and separate from the predator attack and prior electrocution.
active.nextSlice: When Broussard next becomes rotation-eligible, advance the recovery after the predator attack toward restored mobility and eventual convoy return. Preserve the damaged-but-mobile Chimera Two, lost/delayed tow alignment, contracted perimeter, roughly thirty-seven-hour repair estimate, genuine electrocution accident, and unresolved fourteen-second telemetry gap. The deeper falsified-origin/Genestealer truth remains concealed until earned; do not make the predator attack explain it. Apply human-conversation governance and preserve the outcome lock that Broussard ultimately escorts the repaired freighter back to the convoy while the reader eventually sees the hidden Xenos compromise survive. The book may contain no more than 40 chapters.
constraints: Fourteen-second telemetry gap is a surface anomaly, not the main plot hole.
Deep-indexed older telemetry was falsified to conceal the freighter's true port of origin.
Hesperant Vale crew is secretly compromised by Genestealer influence.
Genestealer hybrids are hidden among loose produce bins in the forward holds.
Broussard's detachment successfully returns the damaged freighter to the convoy after fighting additional High Presidio predators.
The reader sees the hidden Xenos travesty continuing beneath the apparent successful rescue.
Recover Google source sequentially and verbatim before fresh expansion.
Jerrik Noll, Edren Vale and Pallas Dorn died by accidental electrocution at an intermittent damaged service-junction cross-feed.
Jerrik was the first casualty; Edren and Pallas died in sequence while trying to help the man ahead of them.
The electrocution is a genuine mundane accident inside the larger mystery and must not be retroactively rewritten as a Genestealer kill.
Broussard still remembers the unexplained telemetry discrepancy after the bodies are recovered.
Hard cap: no book may exceed 40 chapters; Chapter XL is the latest permissible chapter number within a book.

characterContinuityAssessment.segment: XIII. THE THING UNDER THE ICE
characterContinuityAssessment.reason: The chapter materially advances the recovery operation and consumes equipment but does not change the established recurring cast's durable personal knowledge, relationships, injuries, obligations, skills, or long-term plans. Broussard applies already-established survival-focused command competence, Jalesthesian continues established cooperative observation, Kelm continues ship-preservation command, and Sella continues established technical recovery work. The equipment/perimeter consequences are persisted in the circuit rather than manufacturing redundant personal-state entries.

active.title: House Vallimere’s Sons
active.currentEndpoint: Continuation IV — The First Appeal. Eleven days into the one-term assessment pilot, Cadet Commander Solren appeals a failed evaluation after abandoning a damaged troop transport to preserve a refinery and inhabited moon. The review establishes that evaluators must distinguish hindsight disagreement with a command choice from a demonstrated defect in the reasoning available when the order was issued. House Caldrake has a personal stake through a dead officer aboard the transport, but the appeal is resolved procedurally rather than by duel or political capitulation. The Academy codifies the distinction and the pilot continues.
active.nextSlice: On the next House Vallimere rotation, let the one-term pilot generate a new consequence rather than another restatement of the review-board philosophy. Preserve the new appeal precedent: instructor hindsight or moral preference alone is not proof of defective command reasoning. Solren's case remains an institutional example, not an excuse to turn every future chapter into courtroom procedure. Continue the trio's development as teachers and preserve Darcelle's increasing confidence when technical/procedural ground is firm, Renault's restrained humor, Prite's reluctance to reduce doctrine to slogans, the Headmaster's institutional protection, and Vane's Priority Omega role. Shared history should shorten dialogue.

active.title: Matron Lagas Atrovald
active.currentEndpoint: Continuation III — The Record That Waited. Atrovald's S-Rank search finds a possible Witness Two in Mortuary-Seventeen: a sealed remains container whose destruction record says the textual witness was burned, whose mass still matches the ancient certificate, and whose hidden physical inscription says not to destroy it until the first is present. Predulum, without being shown that inscription, reports a fragmentary memory of a furnace, ash and the phrase 'Wait until the first is present.' The missing fifty-third guard acquires a paper-only identity, Custody Auxiliar Hesk Venn, plus an unsigned tomorrow-dated instruction returning him to Null-Seven. Atrovald refuses to sign it and orders future-dated authority treated as evidence rather than instruction.
active.nextSlice: On the next Atrovald rotation, advance the search for Hesk Venn and the provenance of the possible Witness Two without opening or reconciling evidence merely for explanatory convenience. Preserve Predulum's independent furnace/phrase memory, Atrovald's rule that future-dated orders are evidence until issued in ordinary sequence, the unopened Mortuary-Seventeen container, the 53/52 custody discrepancy, Witness Four and Predulum still sealed in Null-Seven, and the unresolved tomorrow-dated accession. Do not explain the anomaly as generic Warp/daemon mechanics. Apply natural-conversation governance: shared facts should shape decisions and shorthand, not be re-recited.

active.title: On the Fuzzy Edge
active.currentEndpoint: Continuation III — Lower Ossuary Nineteen. Javard follows the seventeen-year-pending Ephram Sol transfer through the cathedral underworks. The supposedly sump-condemned route includes a dry containment wall and leads to a clean, apparently occupied niche labeled EPHRAM SOL despite the transfer remaining administratively pending. Ossuary Maintenance Six has stamped annual transfer-readiness inspections on the same liturgical vigil for seventeen years. Javard deliberately leaves the niche unopened. Caldris then reports that the recovering Pontiff Montpclair asked by name whether Interrogator Javard had 'opened Sol,' although Javard never completed his intended introduction. Archive Servitor Nine reacts to Sol by printing 'DO NOT OPEN UNTIL HE ASKS.' Javard chooses to interview Montpclair before disturbing the niche.
active.nextSlice: On the next On the Fuzzy Edge rotation, continue with Javard's interview of the recovering Pontiff Montpclair. Preserve that Sol's niche remains unopened, the old Inquisitorial archive seal remains intact, the Tides of Tomorrow return/register contradiction remains unresolved, Vorn's Graveheart evidence and disputed-reader mark remain live, and neither Javard nor the reader has earned an explanation for who 'he' is or what 'open Sol' ultimately means. Montpclair knows Javard's name and asked whether he had opened Sol before being briefed on the ossuary descent; establish how he knows only through evidence and bounded conversation, not an exposition dump. Maintain Javard's patient procedural method and dry wit as an accent.
